facts: Brown spots with concentric rings in a bull's eye pattern with yellow margin. Fruit gets infected through calyx or stem attachment; brown concentric rings on fruits.

Irregular leaf spots mostly appear from marginal portion of leaves. In many tomato cultivars, symptoms are V shaped and progress towards midrib. facts: Water-soaked black lesions on leaves and stems. Lesions expand rapidly and the entire leaf becomes necrotic. White sporulation on leaves. Dark brown lesions on fruit; soft rot and disintegration of fruits.

Blight appears on foliage as light-pale green water soaked dead area. The lesions are wet in morning and dried, shriveled in daylight. It enlarges rapidly until entire leaves are killed and exposing all the fruits for infection.

In moist and cloudy weather a downy white fungus develops near the outer margin of lesion on underside of the leaves. Green and ripe fruit affected by the blight appear as greenish brown and internal tissues become spongy with bad odour.

Grow resistant variety/hybrid Arka Abhed F1. Avoid planting tomatoes in the same field every year. Remove infected plant parts. Ensure enough space between plants and stake them. Use black polythene mulch (30 micron). Improve field drainage and avoid overhead irrigation. Plant windbreaks and avoid late sowing in the monsoon season.

facts: Severe stunting of plants. Downward rolling and crinkling of the leaves; older leaves become leathery and brittle. Shortened internodes and more side branches give a bushy appearance. The virus is spread by whiteflies (Bemisia tabaci).

Disease appear in severe forms during the month of September to November. Leaves show downward rolling, curling, twisting and chlorosis. Plants show stunting, shortening of internodes, bushy appearance, no flowering and fruiting at later stage of virus infection. Sometimes leaves show light and dark mottle symptoms.

Leaf curl disease is characterized by severe stunting of the plants with downward rolling and crinkling of the leaves. The newly emerging leaves exhibit slight yellow colouration and later they also show curling symptoms.

Raise the nursery under a net of sufficient mesh size to keep out whiteflies. Select seed from disease-free healthy plants. Remove and destroy infected plants in the nursery; do not transplant infected seedlings. In the field: field sanitation, rogue out affected plants, grow maize or sorghum as a barrier crop around the field, use yellow sticky traps @ 10/acre.
answer:
1. The symptoms of tomato leaf curl virus include severe stunting of plants, downward rolling and crinkling of the leaves, and older leaves becoming leathery and brittle.
2. The virus is spread by whiteflies, which are attracted to the plant's sap and can be easily controlled by removing infested plants.
3. The disease appears in severe forms during the months of September and October, and can be controlled by raising the nursery under a net of sufficient mesh size.
4. To prevent the spread of the virus, it is essential to select seed from disease-free healthy plants, and remove and destroy infected plants in the nursery.
